where mv⃗i is the initial momentum and mv⃗f is the final momentum of the body.

The equation (2.26) shows that change in momentum is equal to the product of force and the time for which force is applied. This form of the second law is more general than the form F⃗ = ma⃗, because it can easily be extended to account for changes as the body accelerates when its mass also changes. For example, as a rocket accelerates, it loses mass because its fuel is burnt and ejected to provide greater thrust.

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text: Your hair acts like a crumple zone on your skull. A force of 5N might be enough to fracture your naked skull (cranium), but with a covering of skin and hair, a force of 50 N would be needed.
Thus, second law of motion can also be stated in terms of momentum as:
Time rate of change of momentum of a body is equal to the applied force.
bold: Time rate of change of momentum of a body is equal to the applied force.
